title: God foils a plot over the lost pages with a fuller record
setting: In 1828 Martin Harris lost the first 116 pages of the Book of Mormon translation, which Joseph Smith called the Book of Lehi. By spring 1829 Joseph was translating again at Harmony, Pennsylvania, with Oliver Cowdery as scribe. Nearing the end, they weighed whether to retranslate the lost portion. This revelation told Joseph not to. The date is uncertain: the official heading says most likely April 1829, with parts possibly from summer 1828. The Joseph Smith Papers editors suggest part may have come in 1828 but was written down in 1829.
summary: The revelation reminds Joseph that he lost the writings and his gift by giving them to a wicked man. His gift is now restored, and he is told to pray always and not run faster than his strength allows. It says wicked men have altered the stolen words. Their plan is to wait for a retranslation, then claim the two versions disagree. So Joseph must not translate those words again. Instead he is to translate the fuller account on the plates of Nephi, which covers the same period. The ancient prophets prayed that this gospel would reach the Lamanites and all people in the land. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice defines his church as whoever repents and comes to him.

contextNote.title: Why Joseph would not retranslate
contextNote.text: The revelation describes a trap built around the lost pages. Verses 17–18 lay out the plan: hold altered copies, then claim a new translation contradicts them. Verse 30 forbids Joseph to translate those words again. Verses 38–41 point instead to a fuller account “engraven upon the plates of Nephi” covering the same period. Verse 43 explains the change: God’s “wisdom is greater than the cunning of the devil” and will protect the work. Here wisdom means a second record, already prepared, that makes the plot useless.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 10–11 teaches that the Lord’s wisdom is greater than the cunning of the devil. Read verses 38–45 with Words of Mormon 1:3–7: how was the remedy prepared long before the loss?
reviewNote: Read all 70 verses. Official heading: Harmony, likely April 1829, possibly partly summer 1828; Martin Harris lost the 116 pages; wicked men altered them. JSP historical introduction read for the dating debate (Revelation Book 1 index implies April; 1833 Book of Commandments says May 1829; 1839 history says shortly after July 1828) and the editors’ suggestion of 1828 reception and 1829 recording. Month set to 1829-04 per the heading. Martin Harris is not named in the text but is the person the heading identifies. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
